Definition: from a compound of G4862 and a derivative of G4714; a fellow-insurgent:--make insurrection with.
BiblicalUsage: Mark says Barabbas lay bound with men who had made insurrection with him, rebels who had committed murder in the uprising. The word is for a fellow-insurgent, someone who rose up alongside others. It is the one verse where the King James text carries this word, and the crowd would soon choose Barabbas, the insurgent, over Jesus.
TheologicalSignificance: The contrast is the whole point of the verse, I believe: the crowd freed a man who had risen up with a sword, and handed over the King who would not.
